items.title: Netanyahu says Israel's Iran campaign 'not over' as U.S.-Iran talks begin in Islamabad

featured_image.name: Netanyahu says campaign against Iran 'not over,' admits ...

items.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu declared Saturday night that Israel's campaign against Iran "is not over," issuing a video statement that touted what he called "historic achievements" while acknowledging that "we still have more to do," even as U.S. and Iranian negotiators held their first round of ceasefire talks in Islamabad.[1][2]

items.title: Artemis II crew gets hero's welcome in Houston

featured_image.name: Artemis II Moon Mission: Recovery

items.description: The four astronauts of NASA's Artemis II mission arrived at Ellington Field near Johnson Space Center on Saturday to a thunderous welcome, reuniting with their families for the first time since completing a record-breaking 10-day voyage around the Moon. The crew was greeted with cheers, a standing ovation, and embraces from NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman.[1][2]

items.title: Rubio revokes green cards of Iran hostage crisis spokeswoman's son, family

featured_image.name: ICE detains relatives of 1979 Iran hostage crisis figure after Rubio  revokes their legal status

items.description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio has revoked the green cards of three more Iranian nationals connected to Tehran's ruling establishment, the State Department announced Saturday, expanding a crackdown on regime-linked residents that began the previous week with the detention of relatives of slain military commander Qasem Soleimani.

items.title: U.S.-Iran peace talks begin in Pakistan as Wall Street posts best week since November

featured_image.name: Stock market news for April 8, 2026 - CNBC

items.description: U.S. stocks posted their strongest weekly gains in months as a fragile ceasefire between Washington and Tehran eased fears of a wider conflict and sent oil prices tumbling. The S&P 500 finished the week ending April 10 up roughly 3.6%, its best performance since November, while the Nasdaq Composite surged about 4.7% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 3.6%, returning to positive territory for the year.[1][2][3]

items.title: Altman ties Molotov cocktail attack to New Yorker expose

featured_image.name: Founder Sam Altman Back as OpenAI CEO Under Revamped Board

items.description:
Hours after a 20-year-old man threw a Molotov cocktail at his San Francisco home early Friday morning, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman published a lengthy personal blog post responding to a sweeping New Yorker investigation into his character and leadership — drawing a direct line between the article's rhetoric and the attack on his family.

"There was an incendiary article about me a few days ago," Altman wrote in the post, published April 10. "Now I am awake in the middle of the night and pissed, and thinking that I have underestimated the power of words and narratives."[1]

items.title: GOP lawmakers accuse EU of election meddling in Hungary

featured_image.name: EU Commission presses Hungary to clarify Russia spying allegations

items.description: Two Republican members of Congress sent a letter to European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen on Thursday accusing the EU of "unprecedented, undemocratic interference" in Hungary's parliamentary elections, adding a new dimension to a transatlantic dispute over the vote set for Sunday, April 12.

items.title: US launches mine clearance mission in Strait of Hormuz

featured_image.name: What might a US Navy escort for tankers in the Strait of ...

items.description: Two US Navy guided-missile destroyers transited the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday in the first such passage since the US-Iran conflict began six weeks ago, as US Central Command launched an operation to clear sea mines from one of the world's most critical oil shipping routes.

items.title: Flávio Bolsonaro edges past Lula for first time in Datafolha poll

featured_image.name: Senador Flávio Bolsonaro | Flickr

items.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva finds himself numerically behind Senator Flávio Bolsonaro for the first time in a Datafolha poll, with the latest survey released Saturday showing the right-wing lawmaker at 46% to Lula's 45% in a simulated second-round runoff for the October presidential election. The one-point gap falls within the poll's two-percentage-point margin of error, making it a statistical tie — but the symbolic shift marks a new chapter in what has become one of Brazil's tightest presidential races in years.[1]

items.title: Russia accuses Ukraine of breaking Easter truce minutes after it began

featured_image.name: Russia and Ukraine agree to 32-hour Orthodox Easter ceasefire

items.description:
A Ukrainian drone struck a gas station in the town of Lgov in Russia's Kursk region on Saturday, injuring three people including a child, just minutes after a 32-hour Easter ceasefire announced by President Vladimir Putin took effect, according to regional governor Alexander Khinshtein. The attack, which Khinshtein reported via the messaging platform MAX, occurred shortly after the truce began at 4:00 p.m. Moscow time (1:00 p.m. GMT) on April 11.[1][2]

The incident immediately cast doubt over whether the rare pause in fighting — agreed to by both Moscow and Kyiv for Orthodox Easter — would hold, echoing a pattern from last year's Easter truce when each side accused the other of hundreds of violations.[3][4]

items.title: U.S. Navy ships cross Strait of Hormuz without Iran's approval

featured_image.name: If the US Navy can't open the Strait of Hormuz, it's mad to suggest ...

items.description: Several US Navy ships crossed the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday in a move that was not coordinated with Iranian forces, according to Axios reporter Barak Ravid, citing a US official. The transit marks the first time US naval vessels have passed through the strategic waterway without Iranian approval since the US-Iran conflict began on February 28, representing a direct challenge to Tehran's claim of control over the chokepoint.[1][2][3]

items.title: UAE pulls $3.5B from Pakistan over Iran mediation role

featured_image.name: Pakistan scrambles to meet $4.8 billion dues as UAE seeks ...

items.description: Days before Pakistan helped broker a ceasefire between the United States and Iran, the United Arab Emirates demanded the repayment of a $3.5 billion deposit from Islamabad's central bank — a move that amounted to roughly 21 percent of the country's foreign exchange reserves, according to the South China Morning Post. The withdrawal, which Pakistan's foreign ministry dismissed as a "routine financial transaction," has been widely interpreted as a signal of Abu Dhabi's displeasure with Pakistan's decision to step into a high-profile diplomatic role mediating between Washington and Tehran.[1]

items.title: Iran claims US agreed to unfreeze $6B; White House denies

featured_image.name: Could billions in frozen Iranian assets help the US unlock a ...

items.description: A senior Iranian source told Reuters on Saturday that the United States had agreed to release frozen Iranian assets held in Qatar and other foreign banks, a claim a White House official promptly denied, underscoring the fraught nature of high-stakes diplomacy as U.S.-Iran peace talks got underway in Islamabad.[1][2]

items.title: Iran's new supreme leader has 'severe and disfiguring wounds'

featured_image.name: Iran's new supreme leader has severe and disfiguring wounds ...

items.description: Iran's newly appointed Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei is recovering from serious facial and leg injuries sustained in the February 28 airstrike that killed his father and predecessor, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, according to a Reuters report published Saturday citing three people close to his inner circle. The revelation, which provides the most detailed account yet of his condition, comes as U.S. and Iranian delegations hold historic face-to-face ceasefire talks in Islamabad, Pakistan.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Israel strikes over 200 Hezbollah targets in Lebanon in 24 hours

featured_image.name: Israel hits Hezbollah targets in Lebanon in what it's ...

items.description: The Israeli military said Saturday that it struck more than 200 Hezbollah targets across Lebanon in the past 24 hours, hitting militant infrastructure and rocket launchers as the war between Israel and the Iran-backed group entered its sixth week with no end in sight.

items.title: US-Iran peace talks begin in Islamabad amid fragile ceasefire

featured_image.name: JD Vance arrives in Pakistan for talks with Iranian ...

items.description: French President Emmanuel Macron spoke with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman on Saturday, with the two leaders agreeing on the need to ensure the fragile US-Iran ceasefire is fully respected and extended to Lebanon, according to a headline from CGTN citing Macron's remarks. The call came as US-Iran peace talks got underway in Islamabad, Pakistan, in what officials described as the most direct engagement between Washington and Tehran since the 1979 Islamic revolution.[1][2]

items.title: Iran admits it can't find all mines in Strait of Hormuz

featured_image.name: Iran begins mining Strait of Hormuz as Washington's tanker ...

items.description:
Iran has admitted it cannot locate or remove all of the naval mines it planted in the Strait of Hormuz during its war with the United States, U.S. officials confirmed on Friday, adding a dangerous new obstacle to an already fragile ceasefire and high-stakes peace negotiations set to begin in Islamabad this weekend.[1]

The revelation, first reported by the New York Times, undercuts a central condition of the two-week ceasefire brokered earlier this week: the "complete, immediate, and safe" reopening of the world's most critical oil chokepoint. U.S. intelligence indicates that the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps used hundreds of small boats to mine the strait in a "haphazard" manner after the war began in late February, with many mine locations left unrecorded. Many of the devices have since drifted, rendering Tehran's published "safe route" charts unreliable.[1]

items.title: Israel, Lebanon hold first direct call ahead of Tuesday talks in Washington

featured_image.name: Israel-Lebanon Talks Set at State Dept April 15

items.description:
Israeli and Lebanese diplomats held a preparatory phone call on Friday ahead of the first direct negotiations between the two countries, scheduled for Tuesday, April 14, at the U.S. State Department in Washington, according to multiple officials familiar with the plans.

The call included Israeli Ambassador to the United States Yechiel Leiter, Lebanese Ambassador Nada Hamadeh Moawad, U.S. Ambassador to Lebanon Michel Issa, and State Department Counselor Mike Needham, The Wall Street Journal reported. The conversation aimed to finalize logistics for the in-person meeting, a U.S. official confirmed to The Times of Israel.[1][2]

items.title: Macron invites Trump to Versailles dinner after G7 summit

featured_image.name: Macron Courts Trump with Versailles Invite Ahead of G7 Summit

items.description:
French President Emmanuel Macron has invited U.S. President Donald Trump to a dinner at the Palace of Versailles following the Group of Seven summit in mid-June, though it remains uncertain whether Trump will attend either event, according to a Reuters exclusive report published on Thursday.[1][2]

No other G7 leaders have been invited to the Versailles dinner, which is being framed as a bilateral gesture to underscore Franco-American ties ahead of the United States' 250th anniversary celebrations on July 4.[3][1]

items.title: Jassy defends Amazon's $200B AI bet: 'Not on a hunch'

featured_image.name: Amazon CEO defends AI spend: "We're not going to be conservative"

items.description: Amazon CEO Andy Jassy used his annual shareholder letter, published Thursday, to mount a forceful defense of the company's plan to spend roughly $200 billion on capital expenditures in 2026 — the largest such corporate outlay in history — even as the tech giant continues to shed thousands of jobs.

items.title: Trump's Board of Peace receives fraction of $17B pledged for Gaza

featured_image.name: Trump gets pledges for Gaza reconstruction and troop commitments ...

items.description: Donald Trump's Board of Peace has received less than $1 billion of the $17 billion pledged for the reconstruction of Gaza, according to sources with direct knowledge of the board's operations, leaving the U.S. president unable to advance his plans for the war-torn Palestinian territory.[1][2]
